# Tier-2/3 upstream QEMU backports and two Unicorn fixes (ledger U475-U499), hardware lines only
# (no "=>"): every snippet is our own and runs natively on the host and in Unicorn.
#   emu-alltest --cases Emulator\data\cases_backport_t2.txt --cpuid Emulator\data\cpuid_i5-13600k.txt --strict
# Expected: every line SAME (differing: 0).
#
# --- U476 (backport 7653b44534): SGDT/SIDT store the whole base whatever the operand size. In
# 64-bit mode 66h does not change the 10-byte image (SDM Vol2B SGDT: "the operand size is fixed at
# 8+2 bytes"). The two images are compared on the CPU and the memory is cleared again, so the
# result does not depend on where the host or Unicorn keeps its GDT/IDT: rax = rcx = 0.
sgdt [rsi]; .byte 0x66, 0x0f, 0x01, 0x46, 0x10; mov rax, [rsi+2]; xor rax, [rsi+0x12]; movzx ecx, word ptr [rsi]; movzx edx, word ptr [rsi+0x10]; xor ecx, edx; xor edx, edx; mov [rsi], rdx; mov [rsi+8], rdx; mov [rsi+0x10], rdx; mov [rsi+0x18], rdx
sidt [rsi]; .byte 0x66, 0x0f, 0x01, 0x4e, 0x10; mov rax, [rsi+2]; xor rax, [rsi+0x12]; movzx ecx, word ptr [rsi]; movzx edx, word ptr [rsi+0x10]; xor ecx, edx; xor edx, edx; mov [rsi], rdx; mov [rsi+8], rdx; mov [rsi+0x10], rdx; mov [rsi+0x18], rdx
# the 66h form writes exactly 10 bytes (bytes 10..15 keep their marker)
.byte 0x66, 0x0f, 0x01, 0x06; mov rax, [rsi+8]; shr rax, 16; xor edx, edx; mov [rsi], rdx; mov word ptr [rsi+8], dx | m+0x8008=0000A5A5A5A5A5A5
.byte 0x66, 0x0f, 0x01, 0x0e; mov rax, [rsi+8]; shr rax, 16; xor edx, edx; mov [rsi], rdx; mov word ptr [rsi+8], dx | m+0x8008=0000A5A5A5A5A5A5
#
# --- U480 (backport d3e8b648ab / 4526f58a27 / X86Access series, done by probing): the operand
# ends 'n' bytes into the unmapped page after MEM (#PF on the host; UC_HOOK_MEM_UNMAPPED in Unicorn).
# i5-13600K: FNSAVE / FNSTENV / FXSAVE / XSAVE store nothing, FRSTOR / FLDENV / FXRSTOR / XRSTOR
# load nothing; FSTP m80 / FBSTP store nothing when their low qword crosses the page end, and the
# x87 stack is not popped. Memory before the page end is pre-filled with A5.
# Left out (not repeatable on the i5-13600K, docs/quirks.md "SDM undefined, our choice"): FSTP m80 /
# FBSTP whose low qword ends exactly at the page end store that qword in about 3 of 4 runs and nothing
# otherwise (200 runs each: FSTP 145 / 55, FBSTP 154 / 46); the emulator stores it.
#   fld1; fstp tbyte ptr [rsi+0x7FF8] | m+0xFF00=A5 x 256
#   fld1; fbstp tbyte ptr [rsi+0x7FF8] | m+0xFF00=A5 x 256
fld1; fstp tbyte ptr [rsi+0x7FFA] | 
fld1; fstp tbyte ptr [rsi+0x7FFE] | 
fld1; fbstp tbyte ptr [rsi+0x7FFE] | 
fnsave [rsi+0x7FC0] | 
fnstenv [rsi+0x7FF0] | 
fxsave [rsi+0x7F00] | 
mov eax, 3; xor edx, edx; xsave [rsi+0x7F00] | 
mov eax, 3; xor edx, edx; xsaveopt [rsi+0x7F00] | 
mov eax, 3; xor edx, edx; xsavec [rsi+0x7F00] | 
frstor [rsi+0x7FC0] | m+0xFFC0=7F020000000000000000FFFF
fldenv [rsi+0x7FF0] | m+0xFFF0=7F020000000000000000FFFF
fxrstor [rsi+0x7F00] | m+0xFF00=7F02 m+0xFF18=801F0000FFFF0000 m+0xFFA0=00112233445566778899AABBCCDDEEFF
mov eax, 7; xor edx, edx; xrstor [rsi+0x7DC0] | m+0xFDC0=7F02 m+0xFDD8=801F0000FFFF0000 m+0xFFC0=0700000000000000
# the same images entirely before the page end load / store normally
mov eax, 3; xor edx, edx; xrstor [rsi+0x7DC0] | m+0xFDC0=7F02 m+0xFDD8=801F0000FFFF0000 m+0xFFC0=0300000000000000
fld1; fstp tbyte ptr [rsi+0x7FF6] | 
#
# --- U485 (backport 3fabbe0b7d, UD0/UD1 only): UD0 (0F FF /r) and UD1 (0F B9 /r) are #UD in every form
# (the ModRM-length difference only shows as a fetch fault at a page end: unit test_x86_bp_ud0_ud1_modrm).
.byte 0x0f, 0xb9, 0xc0
.byte 0x0f, 0xb9, 0x46, 0x08
.byte 0x0f, 0xb9, 0x84, 0x24, 0x00, 0x01, 0x00, 0x00
.byte 0x48, 0x0f, 0xb9, 0x05, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00
.byte 0x0f, 0xff, 0xc0
.byte 0x0f, 0xff, 0x46, 0x08
.byte 0x66, 0x0f, 0xff, 0x84, 0x24, 0x00, 0x01, 0x00, 0x00
.byte 0x0f, 0xff, 0x05, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00
#
# --- U486 (backport 183e6679e3): VLDMXCSR/VSTMXCSR with VEX.L = 1 and a W0 form with VEX.W = 1 are #UD
# (the #UD-before-#NM order needs CR0.TS = 1: unit test_x86_bp_vex_ud_before_nm)
.byte 0xc5, 0xfc, 0xae, 0x16 | m+0x8000=801F0000
.byte 0xc5, 0xfc, 0xae, 0x1e
.byte 0xc5, 0xf8, 0xae, 0x1e
.byte 0xc4, 0xe2, 0xf9, 0x0c, 0xc1
.byte 0xc4, 0xe2, 0x79, 0x0c, 0xc1 | xmm0=000000000000803F0000004000004040 xmm1=01000000000000000300000002000000
#
# --- U487 (ours, U70): VGF2P8MULB is W0 only: VEX.W = 1 is #UD; W0 computes
.byte 0xc4, 0xe2, 0xf9, 0xcf, 0xc1
.byte 0xc4, 0xe2, 0x79, 0xcf, 0xc1 | xmm0=0102030405060708090A0B0C0D0E0F10 xmm1=1B53A7FF0280C3E51122334455667788
#
# --- U488 (backport a539cd2614): CPUID 80000000H EBX/ECX/EDX = 0 on Intel (profile mode: the i5-13600K values)
mov eax, 0x80000000; cpuid
#
# --- U489 (backport 8afce497e4): CPUID.80000001H:ECX[8] PRFCHW; PREFETCHW runs
mov eax, 0x80000001; cpuid
prefetchw [rsi]
.byte 0x0f, 0x0d, 0x4e, 0x40
#
# --- U491 (ours) with U482: TF set by POPF single-steps REP MOVSB after its first iteration (#DB with RF = 1,
# U482); the epilogue's PUSHFQ must not copy RF (SDM Vol2B PUSHF). RCX = 3 -> 2, one byte moved.
pushfq; or dword ptr [rsp], 0x100; popfq; rep movsb | rcx=3 m+0x8000=010203
pushfq; or dword ptr [rsp], 0x100; popfq; rep stosd | rcx=4 rax=0x11223344
#
# --- U498/U499 (backport 9f07e47a5e, CPUID part): PCOMMIT withdrawn: 66 0F AE F8 #UD; CPUID 7.0 (profile)
.byte 0x66, 0x0f, 0xae, 0xf8
mov eax, 7; xor ecx, ecx; cpuid
